items.item: Event time and processing time drifting apart isn't a bug to be fixed — it's an inherent property of any distributed system with communication delay, which is exactly why a mechanism like a watermark is needed at all.

at.step: Setup: two needles, one axis

items.item: A watermark being a heuristic rather than a guarantee isn't a weaker version of the same idea — it's a deliberate acceptance that 100% correctness is intractable for most real sources, in exchange for a usable, if imperfect, completeness signal.

at.step: Reveal: a heuristic claim, generated per partition

items.item: Generating a watermark per partition rather than globally isn't an implementation detail — it's the direct cause of the idle-source problem, since a global minimum across partitions is only as current as its least-current member.

at.step: Reveal: a heuristic claim, generated per partition

items.item: Idle-source detection and watermark alignment are solving opposite-signed versions of the exact same underlying issue — one partition lagging behind the group, one partition racing ahead of it — which is why both are bound-based fixes rather than unrelated mechanisms.

at.step: Reveal: alignment bounds the opposite problem

items.item: The latency-completeness trade-off isn't specific to watermarks — it's a specific instance of a trade-off that recurs throughout this chapter whenever a system has to decide how long to wait before declaring something done.

at.step: Reveal: the trade-off, measured

items.item: This topic's hook (one silent partition freezing the whole pipeline) and its fix (an explicit idle timeout) are the same cause and remedy the Flink documentation itself describes, demonstrated here on a toy model rather than a real Flink cluster.

at.step: Hook: one silent partition freezes everything

items.item: The toy synthetic stream, watermark calculator, idle-source model, and alignment model are deliberately simplified standalone demonstrations, not ports of Flink's actual internals, and every figure shown is this run's own measured output, not a cited constant.

at.step: Prove it

items.item: Calling idle-source handling and watermark alignment 'necessary refinements, not edge cases' is a direct consequence of how common both conditions are in real pipelines — an idle partition and an uneven-rate source are the normal case, not the rare one.

at.step: Recap

items.item: A tighter watermark bound isn't simply 'wrong more often' — the events it marks late aren't lost, they're correctly identified as needing a later revision, which is exactly the handling the next cluster of topics covers.
